_comment: create-worktree config for quarterback itself. harness/README.md explains the
keys, harness/worktree.example.json shows every one of them in a single
annotated file, and harness/templates/ holds copyable starting points.
Two choices here are deliberate and worth the note:
docker.enabled=false — docker-compose.yml is TRACKED in this repo, and the
Docker path writes its own compose file into the worktree. That would leave
every worktree permanently dirty and invite committing a generated compose.
Run a worktree's app directly instead: .venv/bin/uvicorn app.main:app
--port $(cat .worktree-port). Postgres is shared from the main checkout's
compose stack; only the database inside it is per-worktree.
database.container=auto — the container is resolved by asking which running
Postgres answers as the URL's user, so this works whatever the checkout
directory (and therefore the compose project name) is called.
base_port starts at 5690 because the main compose stack already publishes
5681 for the app; allocating from 5681 hands a worktree a port it cannot bind.
symlinks is EMPTY and setup builds the venv instead. A symlinked .venv makes
one mutable dependency set serve every worktree: whichever one last ran
`uv pip install` decides what all of them have, and nothing warns. Measured
here on 2026-09-07 at 24 worktrees on one venv across 4 distinct
pyproject.toml files, with the editable .pth pointing at a worktree that was
not the one running — so the MAIN checkout imported another branch's code.
This repo keeps no uv.lock (it is gitignored, deliberately), which makes a
shared venv worse rather than better: two worktrees can resolve different
versions and the last one wins for everybody.
An empty list still means 'use the default', so the key is absent entirely.
The default is [.venv, .claude, CLAUDE.md] filtered to what exists, and this
repo keeps no .claude/ or CLAUDE.md — the agent configuration is global, in
~/.claude. If either ever lands in the repo root, add a symlinks list naming
just that one; do not put .venv back.
Requires a .env in the main checkout (cp .env.example .env). That is the file
create-worktree copies and then repoints at the worktree's own database.
